text:
Logan Stankoven has 13 points in his last ten games, and he's the middle of the best line on the best team in the East. With Nikolaj Ehlers and Jackson Blake he's been on the ice for 14 goals for and one against at five on five.

Some of it is real. Carolina takes 65% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 91st percentile for chances from in front of the net. Some of it isn't: the Hurricanes have scored 9.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his recent ten-game run came on 7.1 expected points. On-ice luck like that fades.

His own shooting is fine. Eleven goals on 10.7 expected, and seven shots on goal at Madison Square Garden on Nov 22.

He's 23, a Stanley Cup winner with Carolina last spring, and on pace to beat his career highs by a distance. What to watch: when the bounces even out, whether the chance creation keeps him producing at a top-six rate.
